<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="חשון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914855_theRebbe_522" batchId="meluket-_D7_97_D7_A9_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914855_theRebbe_522__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the novelty that although teshuvah involves the makifim of Chayah and Yechidah, which are wondrous and distant from Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah, through contemplation within NRN one can awaken these makifim and even the higher makifim of Arich and Atik.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="2">what does the verse innovate in this, that this mitzvah</t>
    <t s="3">(teshuvah)</t>
    <t s="4">is not wondrous for you nor distant from you,</t>
    <t s="5">for seemingly,</t>
    <t s="6">since also in man,</t>
    <t s="7">the service of teshuvah is in the makifim of Chayah and Yechidah,</t>
    <t s="8">which are analogous to the makifim above</t>
    <t s="9">(Arich and Atik),</t>
    <t s="10">what is the innovation</t>
    <t s="11">(so much)</t>
    <t s="12">in this, that through service in the makifim of the soul, the makifim above are drawn down?</t>
    <t s="13">And it may be said,</t>
    <t s="14">that "from you" refers to Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah, which are the essence of man43.</t>
    <t s="15">For although teshuvah is in the makifim of the soul,</t>
    <t s="16">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="17">in order to arouse the makifim, there must be contemplation,</t>
    <t s="18">and the contemplation</t>
    <t s="19">(which is in NRN)</t>
    <t s="20">must be in a manner that through this the makifim that are above intellect will be aroused.</t>
    <t s="21">And this is the innovation in "it is not wondrous for you etc.," that "from you" refers to NRN</t>
    <t s="22">(as above),</t>
    <t s="23">for although the makifim of Chayah and Yechidah are wondrous and distant from NRN,</t>
    <t s="24">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="25">it is within the power of NRN to arouse</t>
    <t s="26">(through appropriate contemplation)</t>
    <t s="27">the makifim of Chayah and Yechidah44,</t>
    <t s="28">and through them also the makifim above,</t>
    <t s="29">Arich and Atik.</t>
    <t s="30">And the reason for this is</t>
    <t s="31">(as brought above</t>
    <t s="32">(end of section 4)</t>
    <t s="33">from the maamar)</t>
    <t s="34">because the souls of Yisrael</t>
    <t s="35">(that is, also the NRN)</t>
    <t s="36">have everything,</t>
    <t s="37">and also from above they are given everything.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the two terms "wondrous" and "distant" in the verse correspond to two aspects of mitzvos: the Divine will beyond reason (wondrous) and the reasons for mitzvos within Chochmah (distant).</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing that the precise explanation of the verse's wording "it is not wondrous from you"</t>
    <t s="2">(specifically "from you"),</t>
    <t s="3">is also according to the interpretation45</t>
    <t s="4">that "this mitzvah" refers to all the mitzvos in general.</t>
    <t s="5">For also according to this interpretation,</t>
    <t s="6">"this mitzvah" is in the category of wonder,</t>
    <t s="7">and as brought above</t>
    <t s="8">(section 4)</t>
    <t s="9">from the maamar,</t>
    <t s="10">that also all the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="11">being the Supernal Will that is above reason,</t>
    <t s="12">are in the category of wonder and distance</t>
    <t s="13">(except that nevertheless it is not wondrous from you,</t>
    <t s="14">from Yisrael).</t>
    <t s="15">And it may be said,</t>
    <t s="16">that this which it says two terms,</t>
    <t s="17">"wondrous" and "distant,"</t>
    <t s="18">is,</t>
    <t s="19">because in mitzvos there are two matters.</t>
    <t s="20">This, that the mitzvos are His will,</t>
    <t s="21">a will that is above reason.</t>
    <t s="22">And this, that after the will becomes clothed in Chochmah</t>
    <t s="23">(of Torah),</t>
    <t s="24">a reason is also added for each mitzvah46.</t>
    <t s="25">And these are the two terms of wonder and distance,</t>
    <t s="26">for the will in the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="27">being above reason,</t>
    <t s="28">is wonder.</t>
    <t s="29">And the reasons for the mitzvos as they are from the aspect of the Chochmah of Torah as it is above,</t>
    <t s="30">are in the category of distance.</t>
    <t s="31">For although also the reasons for the mitzvos</t>
    <t s="32">(as they are in His Chochmah)</t>
    <t s="33">are above the comprehension of human intellect47,</t>
    <t s="34">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="35">the Chochmah above is the source for the Chochmah and intellect of created beings48,</t>
    <t s="36">and therefore it is not wondrous from the intellect of created beings, only distant from them49.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the terms "wondrous" and "distant" only apply after the Torah and mitzvos have descended into a relationship with the world, not in their essential state.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And it may be added,</t>
    <t s="2">that the mitzvos and Torah</t>
    <t s="3">(the reasons for the mitzvos)</t>
    <t s="4">as they are in their own essence,</t>
    <t s="5">it is not applicable to say of them even the description of wonder and distance.</t>
    <t s="6">For the term wonder</t>
    <t s="7">(and certainly the term distance)</t>
    <t s="8">indicates that the wondrous thing has some connection to the thing from which it is wondrous.</t>
    <t s="9">But regarding two matters that have no connection between them,</t>
    <t s="10">the term wonder does not apply.</t>
    <t s="11">Just as it is not applicable to say of a logical concept that it is wondrous from the sense of touch50.</t>
    <t s="12">And that the Torah and mitzvos are distant and wondrous is after they have descended to have some connection to the world.</t>
    <t s="13">For the beginning of the descent is that the Torah preceded the world.</t>
    <t s="14">For the Torah as it is in its own essence,</t>
    <t s="15">is not in the category of worlds at all, and it is not applicable to say of it that it preceded the world.</t>
    <t s="16">And that which our sages said51</t>
    <t s="17">"Two thousand years the Torah preceded the world,"</t>
    <t s="18">is in the level of Torah as it descended52</t>
    <t s="19">to be in the category of worlds.</t>
    <t s="20">For in this level it is applicable to say that it preceded the world,</t>
    <t s="21">and moreover,</t>
    <t s="22">there is a measure to its precedence,</t>
    <t s="23">two thousand years.</t>
    <t s="24">And after this it descended yet many more descents53,</t>
    <t s="25">until it was drawn down below.</t>
    <t s="26">And in this level of Torah,</t>
    <t s="27">as it is after its descent</t>
    <t s="28">[which is a general level,</t>
    <t s="29">including many particular levels,</t>
    <t s="30">from the level of Torah that preceded the world until the level of Torah that was drawn down below]</t>
    <t s="31">it is applicable to say that it is in the category of wonder and distance.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
